entries.desired: Claims distinguish demonstrated results from outlines and unrun comparisons.

sources.verbatim:
\paragraph{What this paper does not claim.}  It does not claim that governing
coding agents this way makes them better.  That comparison has not been run: it
would need an arm in which the same agents work the same codebase without
active-inference-governed selection, adjudicated by someone with no stake in the
outcome, over enough attempts to mean something.  What can be shown, and is
shown here, is narrower and still worth having: that the loop closes, that its
decisions carry reasons a person can inspect and disagree with, and that its
claims about the world are backed by evidence it did not manufacture.  A reader
who finishes this paper believing we have demonstrated benefit has been misled,
and we would rather say so at the start than be read that way.

Two bounds, stated here because they are easier to hold in a paper than in a
meeting. First, the honest claim is \emph{diagnostic, not evolutionary}: that
an organisation instrumented this way will be shown where its decisions are
coupled and where they are not, and \emph{not} that instrumenting it causes
improvement. The selective half of the argument is a plan with criteria fixed
in advance and nothing yet measured; a pitch implying otherwise is claiming an
unrun experiment.

Second, the first engagement is not a validated diagnostic being applied. It is
\textbf{the instrument being built on a real subject}, and it should be scoped
and priced as construction. This is not a hedge --- it is the same claim this
paper makes about itself, applied to the first client rather than to the first
operator.

the invariants: record the decision together with the reasons that produced it;
keep the principled quantities separate from the engineering ones so a reader can
tell which moved a choice; never let a component certify its own output; require
a witness the system could not have manufactured before believing the world has
changed; and treat a failure as terrain to be crossed later rather than as
something to roll back.

entries.desired: The stated invariants are recognisable beyond this one implementation.

sources.verbatim:
A pattern earns its name through repeated enactment and review, and one
implementation in one stack is one enactment; no entrywise promotion census
exists, so this paper makes no numerical or majority claim about which entries
have earned it.

For the pattern reader, the test we cannot run is the one worth running.  If
these invariants are real, they should be recognisable in harnesses built for
entirely different reasons by people who have never read this paper.  Where they
are, the entry has earned its promotion; where they are not, it was a description
of our system all along, and we would rather find that out than not.
